utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Teresa McHenry for the Prosecution, along with Mr. Turone and Mr. Huber. Mr. Niemann is in another courtroom and will be joining us later on today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Edina Residovic, Defence Counsel for Mr. Zejnil Delalic. My co-counsel is my colleague, professor from Canada, Eugene O'Sullivan. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Tomislav Kuzmanovic, along with a legal assistant, Mr. Duric, on behalf of Zdravko Mucic. Mr. Olujic should return next week. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Salih Karabdic, attorney from Sarajevo defending Mr. Hazim Delic. Mr. Hazim Delic is defended also by Mr. Thomas Moran, attorney from Houston, Texas.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I am Cynthia McMurrey representing Esad Landzo. Ms. Nancy Boler our co-counsel should return from Bosnia this afternoon, and joining me today is our legal assistant and attorney from Houston, Texas, Mr. Ken Lindsey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We are starting with the Defence of Hazim Delic this morning. You also said you rearranged the Defence list.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had some transportation problems. Frankly, what happened is they ran out of seats on the aeroplane. It was so tight that our witnesses flew in business class, which makes me very jealous. There should be two more witnesses arriving tomorrow and then our subpoenaed witnesses, we know that the subpoenas have arrived in Bosnia. We have an application for another subpoena. But we can talk about those problems a little later, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I might. I received an order from the court on Friday ordering that I be prepared to answer some questions that the court had about subpoena duces tecum, and I am prepared to discuss that this morning briefly. But also I filed an emergency motion on Friday asking the court to order the Prosecution to disclose the suspects in my case. So sometime today I would like to have that heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will file that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabdic, you start with your first witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I would like to present a brief opening argument, Your Honours. The purpose of this opening argument is to show how to present the basic facts, basic data on the witnesses and other evidence to be led by the Defence, and also to show how this makes part of this whole case. We will thus be making it possible and we will be showing to the Tribunal how to understand and how to interpret our evidence. All the witnesses and the evidence that we will be presenting will aim at contesting and challenging and casting reasonable doubt on the evidence presented by the Prosecution. The evidence presented will, first of all, relate to the basic facts alleged in the indictment, the general allegations, and also the allegations concerning all the accused and, in particular, the first three of the accused. Our evidence will show that the arrests that took place in the Municipality of Konjic, the arrests of persons later to be detained in the Celebici prison, were carried out because these persons did not obey the laws of the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina because they illegally carried weapons, they attacked legal armed forces, and prevented the freedom of movements on roads, and both the general allegations and the particular charges relating to the illegal detention of civilians, that all will be refuted. Our witnesses will be talking about that, Cosic, Ramic and Djajic. We will in particular refute the allegations of the Prosecution and their witnesses, who claim that these persons were not Bosnia citizens. We will call Ms. Amira Klaric, she is the registrar of the Konjic municipality, and she is the custodian of the registries of births, deaths and marriages, and also of citizenship in the Municipality of Konjic. Her testimony will show that all the persons indicated herein as victims or mentioned in the indictment or who testified here as witnesses and other persons mentioned in documents tendered here by the Prosecution, it will show that these persons are all citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the relevant times. In particular, Ms. Klaric will be presenting over 180 documents relating to the registries of births and citizenship and marriages. This all relates to the Prosecution witnesses and persons mentioned in the indictment. We will also call witnesses who will prove that in the Celebici prison, that the conditions in the Celebici prison were as good as possible under the circumstances prevalent at the times. We will prove that prisoners got the food the same as other citizens, and the same amounts of food as the soldiers at the frontlines. We will prove that they had adequate water supply, that they had visitation rights, and that they had the right to be visited three times a week, that they had medical care. Again, I stress under the conditions prevalent at the time in Konjic, the medical care was as good as could be provided. Our witnesses, Dzajic, Ibrahimi, Sevajdin and others, will be talking about that. Furthermore, we will call an expert witness, Dr. Eduardo Bellas, as a forensic pathologist. He will testify relating to the credibility of many of the Prosecution witnesses. Dr. Bellas examined portions of the transcript and he will continue to do so, and other parts of the transcript that we will submit to him where Prosecution witnesses described numerous injuries and the conditions in the camp. We expect that Mr. Bellas will be testifying to the effect that, on the basis of his knowledge and experience, that many Prosecution witnesses, that their testimony was not credible or exaggerated. The Defence will furthermore present witnesses and lead evidence regarding the defendant, Mr. Hazim Delic. We will call Dr. Buturovic, who should testify about injuries sustained by Mr. Delic, and his ability to walk and work in the months relevant for the indictment. We will also, in particular, call witnesses who will challenge the testimony of Grozdana Cecez and Milojka Antic, the witnesses who, according to those two, were present during the events that they had testified about, and the testimony of our witnesses will refute the statements of those two Prosecution witnesses. Our witnesses are Cosic and Ibrahimi as to that fact. So that would be, briefly, all I have to say, and, with your permission, I would now like to call witness Ziam Cosic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. While we are waiting, our LiveNote transcript is not working over here. I think it's merely unplugged. If I could have technical assistance on that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Swear the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I suggest it be read aloud in English, then it can be translated and then he can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Witness, if you could repeat me. I solemnly declare --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: If I may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Karabdic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Salih Karabdic, I am the Defence Counsel for Mr. Hazim Delic. I will be asking some questions, but before I start to examine you, I would like to warn you of certain facts and give you certain instructions of a technical nature. Both you and I, we speak the Bosnian language and we could be asking questions and giving answers rather quickly. However, in accordance with the rules and the statute of this Tribunal, all the testimony is interpreted into English and French and it takes time to do so. And that's why I would like to ask you not to give your answer immediately, but to wait a while, after I finish asking the questions, and then to give your answer. Many of the questions you will be able to answer with just "yes" and "no," but, please, don't do so by nodding your head, but indicate clearly and loudly "yes" and "no," because every word here is being recorded, and the ladies in charge of that are unable to note down your nodding. Will you please give your full name to the court.

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: My name is Ziam Cosic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you born and where?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I was born on the 30th of September, 1956, in Idbar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where do you live?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I reside at Idbar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: My ethnic background is Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your citizenship?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your marital status? Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I am married, father of five.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your education?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I finished my primary education in Celebici and graduated from high school in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a high school?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Carpentry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do your national service in the JNA, and if yes, please tell us when and where.

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I started my national service on the 13th of December, 1975, and I served in the JNA until the 3rd of March, 1977. Yes, that's right, 1977.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you serve your national service?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: In Prizen. That's in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, the television screen that normally shows what's happening in the courtroom when we are in public session is flickering, and I am not sure whether we are in a public session or in a private session. We are supposed to be in public session. I said I would inform the court of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While in the JNA, did you have any special functions?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I graduated from a school in Prizen. That was for the squad leader. And then I was appointed to the function of the commander of the watch tower Stojanovac at the Yugoslav Albanian border. And then I was given the rank of Vodnik. That's Corporal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came back from the army, naturally, as everybody else, you had to report to your military department. Were you assigned to a certain duty or a certain post?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I was assigned combat post in the municipal headquarters in Konjic, the municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Would you kindly please go to the type of evidence he is here to give. It is not an issue in this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I will strive to ask questions, but it seems to me that this would be also important for the understanding of the ensuing events. But, thank you, Your Honours, for your caution. I will try.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you lived in the village of Idbar. How large is this village? How many inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Until the war, my village had around 120 households and around 400 inhabitants. About 15 households were Serbian, three Croatian, and the rest were Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the geographical location of the village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Idbar is in a valley surrounded by hills on all sides, and there is a nice river flowing from Idbar to Celebici. And the only route is the canyon of the ^ Bastovic River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told me that there were several people of several ethnic backgrounds in your village before the war. What were the relations between those various nationalities in your village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The relations were good until that time when the Serbs held some kind of a plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, what happened in April, 1992, in your village and in the surrounding areas? What contributed to the changes in the circumstances and the conditions?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: In early April, right at the beginning, Serbs left. All the state authorities, such as the Territorial Defence, the Ministry of the Interior, they refused to recognise the independent state of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like you to limit your answers to your village. What happened in your village and the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, in the village itself there was disorder. Roads were blocked by the Serbs, because between my village, my hamlet and Celebici, there is a Serbian hamlet, and they refused to participate together with us in the defence of our country against the aggression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you organise in your village in relation to these events?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It wasn't easy. For us, this was something completely abnormal and it was difficult to find your way around in a situation like this when Chetniks came from Nevesinge in the neighbouring Village of Bijela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did these Chetniks behave in the Village of Bijela and what kind of influence did this have on your village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Three young men immediately left our village --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Don't you think we'll be much more interested in Delic than the experience of this witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, I will try to do that, but, believe me, I will -- I am also trying to present all the things that have to do with general allegations, but I will try to be as short as possible. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We've heard so much from so many witnesses about general disorganisation, about that area, about that time. I don't think he can add more to what all those who were actually participating in it could say. We're here interested in the Defence of the witness you've called, not of this witness, but of the accused person who is here to be his witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour, it is true that many have spoken about that here because many have been witnesses here, a couple of generals, brigadiers, commanders. This is a man from the village, from life. And this man should tell us about this life. I wanted him to tell us what it was like on the ground. But, Your Honour, this is what it's about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I will certainly try to that. I can't do it immediately, but all this is Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cosic, did you in the village find out that the other inhabitants, the Serbs, are buying arms?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you find out about that?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: In the hamlet, which was mostly inhabited by the Serbs, there are two Bosniak families and they watched these things happening over night and they were telling this to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please come directly to the point, your Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a Territorial Defence unit formed in the village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who decided that you should be the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The commander of the battalion, Sefik Omerovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many members did your unit have in your unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Please be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I will try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is totally irrelevant. How are we interested? How does it prove or disprove the allegations against you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't want to disrespect you, but I would like to say that this witness will present the circumstances that -- about the arming and buying of weapons. And this later has a lot to do with the arrest. And with due respect, Your Honours, this is relevant to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabdic, the Prosecution has given evidence and the Defence has substantially corroborated what happened during that period. Now what you are concerned in the Defence of Delic is the specific allegations made against him. Whatever you are now saying should be related to those specific allegations. The general allegations are there and I think you cannot change them. I think even if you add to them, it may not make much of a difference to them. But specific allegations which you have called this witness to come and disprove is what we want to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Did he himself arrest any of the detainees? Ask him. Under what circumstances did they arrest them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will come to that point. With all due respect, Your Honours, I must say that the Defence of my client, Hazim Delic, for concrete allegations cannot be separated from the Defence and from the general circumstances that were present at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You're trying to show that the detainees were carrying arms, they were rebels against the authorities. Did he arrest any of them? And under what circumstances did he arrest them? Please ask him straight away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, I will pose this question after a number of introductory questions and I would like to ask you to let me ask a couple of more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If you have introductory questions to ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: We will come to direct events after a couple of questions. We will finish very soon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many members were there in your unit of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: About a hundred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Eight rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do to procure those hunting rifles? What did you do first? Did you try to buy those weapons from somebody?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I don't know. The higher command was doing these things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the Villages of Turije, Zaslivlje and Zabrdje with regard to this?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We went to Ljubina because of the weapons, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was there in those three villages?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: HVO was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you reach an agreement with them, with regard to the weapons and joint actions?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, we did. They were to give us 14 weapons -- 14 rifles and uniforms and we were to hold our positions together in Ljubina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to Ljubina and when?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I went to Ljubina for the first time on the 30th of April and then, after that, this position was important throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see from Ljubina? What was happening in the other villages, in the villages of Bijela and others?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: From Bijela you can see Konjic, Bijela, Orahovica, Celebici, Idbar, Toria, Salsia (phoen) and all the other villages. And I saw that the Serbs were burning everything that was non-Serb. They burned a factory, a saw mill in -- which was, which was owned by the Croats, I think it was in Vidackovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that some houses were burning and whose houses were those?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Houses belonging both to Bosniaks and Croats were burning, everything which was burning was non-Serb was burning by the Chetniks. And at night, their houses -- some houses and some villages would use some light signals and all this was very confusing for us. And they had some signals with which they would communicate amongst each other within our villages and amongst the Serbs and their military formations which were attacking us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the attack on Ljubina? And did you get any notice of this beforehand?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The information about this we received from Esad Ramic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: He said that the Chetniks from Bijela would attack us on Ljubina and that we must strengthen our forces. And then immediately that night we went with more people and there were already soldiers in Ljubina, but we strengthened our forces at night. And this night was the night between the 6th and the 7th and the battle took place around noon, they attacked us on the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Of which month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of May. On the 7th of May, the battle took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the result of the battle?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The result was we had four dead: one Bosniak and three Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the -- and could the Chetniks pass?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, they could not. No, they did not pass that time because we managed to throw them back if they had passed then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is what you think would have happened. When you came to the Village of this event, what did you find out, what happened in the village during the time you were away?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: While we were in Ljubina, a patrol came to the village. I found out about this in the evening when I came back. This patrol belonged to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, to the police and the military police and HVO and they searched the village and they found the weapons. They found some weapons in the Serb houses who lived in the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what kind of weapons were found?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: They found one machine gun, M-53, and some M-48s, rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any of the weapons from those weapons that were seized, your unit?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, Rale brought me six rifles from all that ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned Rale, was Rale in this patrol that searched the village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I was not in the village when they were searching it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know what kind of ammunition you got at this time?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes. I noted it on the 29th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But at this time, what kind of weapons were these six rifles that you got?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: A machine gun was found at Simo Jovanovic's. It was an M-53 and then other rifles, M-48, military rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to those Serbs, in whose houses where these weapons were found?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I don't know what you are trying to do, whether this has, in any event, any connection with the accused person himself. How does all these things concern him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be shown shortly. My weapons -- my defendant, Your Honours, with all due respect, I must say that my defendant has also been charged with unlawful detention of civilians and for everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If arrested any of the detainees and there were circumstances, he arrested them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Not this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: You are talking about generally what happened. You're talking about detainees in the Celebici camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, did those people, were those people arrested, those people in whose houses you found weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The police took them away on the 9th of May, after the barrel of my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as I understand, they were not taken away immediately, but on the 9th of May the police came to get them?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was arrested as far as you can remember? Who was taken away from you village at that time, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: They took away Vojo Jovanovic, Mirko Antic, Cedo Antic. Simo tried to escape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which Simo?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Simo Jovanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened with Simo?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: They caught up with him at Prenj, the members of the police and they took him to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of weapons were found at Simo Jovanovic's?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I already said that, M-53s, a light machine gun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find any weapons after this event in your village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, on the 28th of May and on the 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under whose command was this done and who found these weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: They came from the police, Dzevad Alibasic and Almir Mulic. They are members of the police and were responsible for Idbar. And in cooperation with Sefik Omerovic this was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was found at this time?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: At this time I wrote it down. On the 28th of May, a rifle, a PAP rifle, it's a semi-automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: May I? Just excuse me. I see that the witness is reading from a document and I would just ask Defence counsel to provide us a copy of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He said he wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I am not objecting, I am just asking for a copy for us to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Yes, we will provide a copy immediately at the break. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: So one semi-automatic rifle, No. 352127. It was found at Jovanovic Krijk (phoen). Rifle No. M-48, 130-41. Also found in a shed next to the house, which belonged to his son, Velimir Jovanovic, we wrote Rajko Jovanovic. And some bombs, two pieces, hand bombs, and a lot of ammunition, uniforms and crates. And on 29th we found an M-48, 630-28 rifles at Cedo Antic's. And then he said later, Omerovic told me so, that this was a gun which belonged to Mirko Antic. A rifle, M-48, 250-80, Ilija Jovanovic, a hunting rifle, 731-444, found at Milovan Jovanovic. A rocket launcher, M-55, 890 at Savo Antic's and one crate of mines. This was found at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these persons arrested?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, not at this time, after about a fortnight. Alibasic and Muhic came and we were surrounding the territory and then they went in. And they took them to the fishery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Milojka Antic arrested at this time?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Probably because her brother told her that it was her rifle that they found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that these people were taken to the fishery next to the village, who took them over there?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: A person -- a truck -- a tram took them there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these people maltreated and were they abused during the arrest? How were they treated?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, nobody was maltreated. On the contrary, we protected them to avoid any maltreatment of these people because these were our neighbours that we lived with and worked with and cooperated with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were they taken?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I don't know. I never interested myself in these people ever again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that they were taken to Celebici camp?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know where they were taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, generally speaking, have you ever been in the barracks, Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, I never entered. Through this gate, I see it in front of me, it seems that this is -- we went there in August to -- for a solemn declaration, but from the other side. I never entered the camp through the main gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of a solemn swearing was this?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It was the declaration for the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this event, did you ever go to the barracks, Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: This is all, Your Honours, I have finished with the examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Have you any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Defence counsel for Mr. Delalic has no questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Defence for Mr. Mucic has no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions from Landzo's corner?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we have a few brief questions. May I question from here? Thank you. Cross-examined by Ms. McMurrey

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cosic. I am Cynthia McMurrey and I represent Mr. Esad Landzo. And we have never had an opportunity to speak before, have we?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are from the Village of Idbar; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Village at Idbar, I believe, is about 120 households and out of the 120 households, about fifteen of those were considered Serb households, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your testimony just a moment ago, you testified that the Serbs that were arrested in Idbar, they were taken to a fishery. Now, the fishery you're referring to is the business owned by Simo Jovanovic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, in Idbar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified that Mr. Jovanovic was arrested because he had really collected a fairly large arsenal of weapons on his property, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Javanovic in Idbar was considered a wealthy man, was he not?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, there were some Muslims who were rich.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, by the standards in the village, he had a business and he had a home, and so, by most of the standards, he would be one of the wealthier citizens in the village of Idbar? Would that be accurate or not?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, yes, relatively speaking, because he was given some loans by the municipality, some agricultural loans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that once he was arrested and sent to Celebici, you don't know what happened to Mr. Jovanovic after that point, do you?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to his property in Idbar?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The house still stands, and we have our school there, because our real school was destroyed by the Chetniks. The fishery still stands. Everything is there just as it used to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so would it be fair to say that the people of Idbar, basically, took over the property of Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, in a certain sense, yes. It is being guarded, because the school is in that house.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cosic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any questions from the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I can either start now and then during the break review the piece of paper, or we can take the break now and I will do everything all at once. It's up to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can start now. The piece of paper merely reinforces his memory.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. McHenry

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you say Mr. Jovanovic's house is being guarded, what do you mean by that? Are you suggesting that his house is being guarded in safekeeping for Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He answered that. He said they are running a school there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes. That's right, he answered it, but he also said then it was being guarded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree that the house and the other belongings of Mr. Jovanovic have been taken over by the village of Idbar and are not being kept for the use of Mr. Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object. That's asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has answered. He did say in some sense, yes, because they are using this building for the school. His answer still stands as they have always been. That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that Mr. Jovanovic has no chance of ever getting any of that property back, does he?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: (Microphone not on) -- they can go back and take over the property. He already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I object to this line of questioning. This is a question relating to the peace accords and the return of the refugees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I may be allowed to answer. In our parts, the private property is sacrosanct. His wife went there recently. It's her private property. Nobody has any right to that. It's just his and his wife's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware, sir, aren't you, that Mr. Jovanovic was murdered in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to object. He said he didn't know what happened to the Serb detainees once they left Idbar, number one; and number two, that has not been proven in this case. That's an issue for the court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think you are quite correct. That was his answer. He didn't know what happened to him thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Fine. Sir, I will move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The answers of the witnesses -- when you are cross-examining, if the answers are clear and not contradicted so far, you don't have to cross-examine him on that. He's answered it properly and I don't see the point in asking him for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, after he was arrested and taken to Celebici, you've never seen Mr. Jovanovic again, have you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He said that he was taken to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I believe he said he was one of the people who was --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, after Mr. Jovanovic was arrested and taken away, have you ever had an opportunity to see him again?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, I never saw any of those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were talking about in the beginning, when Mr. Karabdic was asking you about the background and you talked about some Chetniks from Bijela. Is Bijela part of Konjic or not?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it, sir, your opinion, at the time that these persons were arrested, that the Serbs in Idbar who were arrested were part of the Serb forces attacking Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you talked about some weapons that were taken, and you initially talked about some weapons that were taken on the 9th of May. Now, first of all, are you sure that it was the 9th of May or was it the 20th of May?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The weapons seized before the 9th of May, and on the 9th of May they were taken away, after my father's funeral.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- let me go on. And some of those weapons were legal hunting weapons that were found at that time, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Those who had hunting weapons in Idbar, such as Djordjo Jovanovic, Ilija Jovanovic, they immediately joined the Chetniks in Bijela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was: In addition to the -- whatever weapons you've already testified about, you would agree with me that some of the weapons that were found were legal hunting weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: In accordance with the law on hunting, one is not allowed to have mortar, sniper rifles, military weapons, automatic weapons and things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question was: Were there any legal hunting weapons found?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: One hunting rifle was found at Mirko's.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before my colleague continues, I would like to warn that in this transcript on several occasions, instead of the name of the village of Bijela, we have the name of the mountain, which is quite far away from this area, the mountain of Bjelasnica. So I would like to have this corrected, Bijela, not Bjelasnica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, with respect to the weapons that were seized on the 9th of May, you weren't present and you have no personal knowledge about any of that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, am I correct that you weren't there and you have no personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I have knowledge from what Rale told me and the six pieces of weapons that he brought me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time did Rale tell you from whose house every single weapon came from?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you write that down or you just -- are you just testifying from your own memory from what he told you in 1992?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, from my recollection, but also because I immediately issued those weapons to my soldiers, and that's how I know about those weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, sir, would you agree with me that previously you stated that Mr. ^ Spasoje Jovanovic, Mr. Mirko Antic, Mr. ^ Rado Antic, all had hunting rifles that were taken at that time?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: They had those weapons, but they never were hunters. They were able to obtain all kinds of weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that they were normally considered hunting weapons, but because they weren't hunters, you don't consider them hunting weapons; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Not in Bosnia, because nobody in Bosniak can have weapons if they are not hunters and if they don't have the licence to have those weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would also agree with me that previously you gave a statement in which you indicated that all this happened on the 20th of May, not the 9th of May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No. On the 9th of May. This is when they were taken away, not on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also testified about some weapons that were seized on the 28th and 29th. Were you present when those -- all those weapons were seized?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you indicated that there was an M48 that you later heard had been taken from -- had been issued to Milojka Antic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that M48 found?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It was found next to a place where meat is cured. It was buried in the flower bed next to the place where the meat is dried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you actually present when it was uncovered?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes. Sefik Omerovic was with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the time when you wrote down the serial number? Is that the time that you wrote down the serial number of that M48?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the serial number of that M48 that you found on May 28th or 9th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when was it that somebody told you that that was Mrs. Antic's rifle?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: A day or two later Omerovic told me that this was a rifle belonging to Milojka Antic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ask Mr. Omerovic who told you about this? Did you ask him how he knew of that?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Mr. Omerovic was the commander of the detachment and he sometimes had consultations with the Ministry of the Interior and the chain of command from the staff to the smallest unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I take it, sir, that you have no idea how Mr. Omerovic, where he received this information?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, probably at the barracks in the Celebici barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you, yourself, have no information about where he received it, and you are just guessing?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, I don't know, because all the weapons were immediately issued to the soldiers. We, as the Territorial Defence, did not really think about it. We had more serious tasks, such as the defence at Ljubina, Orahovica, Turije, Prenj and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Mrs. Antic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And she would be a middle-aged woman who lived with her elderly mother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, if she had gotten married, she would probably have been a mother.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The question was whether she lived with her mother in Idbar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, she did. She lived with her mother and her brother. They were next door neighbours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let me go back. When you say that Mr. Omerovic was commander of the detachment, what detachment are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: That wasn't a platoon, that was the Ljubina detachment. It was composed of several companies or units, the Orahovica, Celebici, Zabrdje and Idbar. So he was the commander of the larger unit, subordinate -- super ordinate unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was your superior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and everyone else in your unit have a uniform, wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: We had uniforms. Not all of us, but we -- so whoever was at the line had to be in a uniform. We had about 15 uniforms, so we would take turns wearing the uniforms. As soon you got onto the line, defence line, you put on the uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what kind of insignia did the uniforms have?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence insignia. Some people did have those insignias, some didn't, depending on the availability.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me move forward. It was you personally who arrested Ms. Antic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who actually arrested Ms. Antic then?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Dzevad Alibasic and Almir Mulic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you the third person present at the time she was arrested?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Myself and Omerovic followed them, because our unit provided the security, the guards around the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And Mrs. Antic talked to you when she was arrested, because you were the only person she knew; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No. She knew other people too, but they did not live there. Alibasic lived in Celebici and Almir lived in Konjic, and that's why she talked to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did she say to you?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: She asked me how long she would be staying there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: She asked you how long she would be staying at Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Not in Celebici. Celebici was not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when she asked you how long would she be staying there, what "there" was she referring to?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Didn't she ask you whether or not she could go inside and change her clothes also, and you told her "no"?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, she did not ask me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did she ask that something be done to take care of her elderly mother?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No. No, she did not ask me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there a search done of Ms. Antic's house at any time when you were present, or in the area?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, we did not enter houses because her rifle was found in the yard next to the place where the meat was dried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did anyone -- what was told to Mrs. Antic about why she was being arrested?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Was he the person who arrested her?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: He said he was present at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, what was told to Mrs. Antic about why she was being arrested?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: She was told that this matter will be examined by some kind of a commission, and that if she were to be found guilty, she would be detained for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was you who told Mrs. Antic that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I told her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you -- did you -- did you tell her that she was suspected of having a transmitter?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell her that she was suspected of having a gun?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, because it was not our business. This was up to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would agree with me that Mrs. Antic wasn't told anything about why she was being arrested?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Nobody told her anything about that beforehand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, is it your testimony that at this time you had no idea whatsoever that Mrs. Antic was being -- was going to be brought to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Is it your testimony that at this time you had no idea whatsoever that Mrs. Antic was being brought to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Well, the only place she could have gone to by car from Idbar was Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to ask that the witness be shown Defence Exhibit 1 -- D145/A7-31. While you are looking for it, let me just go forward. Sir, did you ever receive any information that any other weapons were found in Idbar after the 28th and 29th?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: We may be able to short circuit some of this process. We are about to introduce through another witness that document for the truth of the matter asserted. And I have extra copies for the court. So that the court can have them, we can just hand them out now, so that you know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: No, no the direction of this cross-examination ends first.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: I think we are going to have our break in a few minutes and maybe we can get the document then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, after the 28th and 29th, do you have any information that any other weapons were ever found in Idbar?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were the other weapons found?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I don't know when it was, precisely, but members of the MUP and the HVO military police came and they searched the place. We, as the Territorial Defence, had nothing to do with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, going back to the rifle that was found that you later heard had belonged to Milojka Antic. Whose chicken coop was it found near? Was it on Ms. Antic's property or not?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, on the property of Milojka Antic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever -- and did you ever learn whether or not there were any other weapons found on that same property?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I heard that another rifle was found, but I don't know anything about that rifle because it never reached my company, my unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if this is time for the break, I think when I come back I'll just have one or two additional questions and then be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble at noon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Please remind the witness he's still on his oath.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still under oath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, previously, you would agree with me, that you stated that you and other members of the TO arrested Miloka Antic on the 29th of May, 1992; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you've stated previously that you and other members of the TO arrested Miloka Antic on the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The TO didn't arrest anybody. They only guarded the village, the area around the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, is it correct that previously in a written statement you gave to the Defence, you stated that it was you and other members of the TO who arrested Mrs. Antic and that it happened on the 29th of May?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: That is not correct and it did not happen on the 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I just ask that the witness be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You want him to say that he's never said that or it never happened like that? He's now saying that that is not the fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: But you're saying that he said that to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I put a yellow sticker, just to help you, sir, direct you to the portion that I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked 253.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask that you look at the document that you've been given. Sir, is this a copy of a statement that you previously gave to a Defence investigator?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, but it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I am going to direct you to where the yellow sticker was, and can you tell me if it states that "On the 29th of May, 1992, on a verbal order of Sefik Omerovic, commander of the Ljubina unit, I and a group of TO members remanded in custody, the following persons?" And then one of the names is Mrs. Antic. Sir, is that what the document says?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It says in the document, but she wasn't arrested at that time and neither were these other people. This is a mistake of the person who was writing this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And since then, have you talked to anyone who reminded you of the correct date?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, sir, you would agree with me that you've talked about your testimony with Defence investigators before you came here, with Defence representatives, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Only with Nehir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it your testimony, sir, in the statement where it says that you were the one who arrested Mrs. Antic, is that a mistake also?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It is a mistake, the Territorial Defence did not arrest anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have a chance to read that statement before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I thought there was no need and I only signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me go back, sir, to a different question. I have no more questions from this document. You would agree with me that the notes you took on the 28th and 29th of May, that you were looking at during your direct testimony, you would agree that there's nothing in those notes that indicates that any weapon found had anything to do with Miloka Antic; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: We wrote that and we stated that as if the weapons belonged to her brother, but Omerovic told me later that her brother said that the weapon belonged to Miloka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, I am just clarifying that the records you took at the time don't mention anything whatsoever about Miloka Antic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It is not mentioned in the notes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you would also agree with me, sir, that on the 28th and the 29th, you and the soldiers and other military persons, took a large amount of food and some alcohol from Serb families living in Idbar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you would agree with me that your notes indicate that a large amount of food and some alcohol were taken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, it is not. Everything was outside of the houses, the TO only searched the area and nobody went into any of the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, when it talks about in addition to some weapons, when it talks about 100 kilos of potato, and sugar, 90 kilograms of potatoes and sugar and flour and brandy being taken, where were those things taken from?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: These things were taken from some sheds, bunkers, outside of the houses, none of this was found inside the houses, nobody entered the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, sir, that then a large amount of food and some alcohol was taken from the Serb families in Idbar, even if it wasn't taken, according to you, from their houses; Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It did not belong to the Serb families, it was not taken from them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did it belong to, sir?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It probably belonged to the military formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you determine that, sir, that it belonged to the military formations and not the families?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: We did not determine that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination, please? You have no re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I have. Re-examined by Mr. Karabdic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, this food that has been mentioned, was this food found together with the weapons that you found, did you find the food next to the weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, not next to the weapons. The food was found outside of the houses in bunkers and the weapons were usually dugged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since the food was hidden, is that how you concluded that this food was prepared for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: It served for military purposes, for logistics of their gangs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You also mentioned that you saw in Bijela that some Chetnik forces attacked you in Bijela, could you tell us what kind of forces these were and how were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: They wore olive green/grey uniforms belonging to the JNA. On their heads they had caps, high rising caps, fur hats and they had (no translation) on the caps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, when Simo Jovanovic was taken away from Idbar, what happened to his family?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: They stayed there to live normally, his father and his mother and his wife.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they take care of his property?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, they did, his father and his mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, could you tell me, if there were Serbs in Idbar who spent the whole time with you?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They did not have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, they did not have weapons. Those who stayed there for the whole time did not have any weapons. And there are still Serbs living with us today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: This did not an arise from cross examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may interrupt for a moment. Page 46, line 17, the marking on the cap was not translated, I believe the witness had said there were skull and crossbones marking on the cap and that is not in translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your correction. Thank you very much, Mr. Cosic, I think this is all for you. You are discharged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You can now leave. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Mr. Karabdic, can you call your next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: I would like to call the witness Ramic, Agan. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Kindly let the witness take the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may take your seat, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: RAMIC AGAN Examined by Mr. Karabdic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Salih Karabdic and I am defending Mr. Hazim Delic. I would like to ask you a couple of questions, but before that, I would like to give you a few instructions. Since the official languages are English and French, everything that the two of us will be speaking in the Bosnian language, will have to be translated into one of the two official languages. This takes time, therefore, I would like to ask you not to hurry and to wait for a while until my questions are interpreted and then to reply and to reply slowly. Do not give your answers by nodding or by doing something else. If you would like to say "yes" or "no", please say so. Whatever is uttered here in this Court must be written down in the transcript. Did you understand this?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please say your name?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: My name is Ramic, Agan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I was born on March 17th, 1962.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where do you live?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: In Brdani, Municipality of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at the beginning of the war, that is to say on April the 6th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I was in Brdani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you engaged in the defence?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which unit did you join?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: We were an independent platoon which belonged to the detachment of Zupcanik. We actually belonged to the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the process of mobilisation, did all citizens respond to this mobilisation, including the citizens of Serbian nationality?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: No, not all citizens joined the mobilisation. People who were Serbs did not respond to this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any information that persons of Serb nationality were armed?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We had some information that they were armed. And this is precisely the reason, precisely for this reason we decided to organise ourselves and also to arm ourselves and to prepare.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of this unit of yours in your village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: I was the commander. And the overall commander, the commander of the detachment that we belonged to was Mr. Zavko (sic).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you try to reach an agreement in a peaceful way with the citizens of Serb nationality with respect to the outbreak of the war, so that you would not attack each other and defend the village together?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Several times we negotiated with people of Serb nationality. And the members of the municipality staff of TO have suggested at those times to the Serbs to join the units of TO or to hand in the weapons that they have if they don't want to join.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before my colleague continues there is a mistake in the transcript. The question stating who was the commander. The response said Mr. "Zavko". The witness stated another name and it would be good to say again who this commander was, who was the commander of his detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: You heard, could you please say what his name was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Zovko, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He said that he was the commander of his village, but the overall commander, the name of the overall commander was written in the wrong way and I would like to say that the witness restates the name of the overall commander so that this can be changed in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Okay, ask your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have heard the statement. Please, who was the commander of the detachment that your unit belonged to, your unit in the village?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The commander was Zvonko Zovko and his headquarters were in Podgradac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't fully hear your response, your attempts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let's not get the name again because it doesn't sound right from what I read here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you, please, clearly state the name of the commander of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The commander of the detachment was Zovko, Z-o-v-k-o, Zvonko, Z-v-o-n-k-o, and the headquarters was in Podgradac.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The name is Zvonko Zovko and maybe the interpreter does not get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Well, it might not be that important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It might be. I think, let's get it correct, let's know what the name is. It's important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the usher please hand a piece of paper to the witness so that he could write down the name with the correct spelling, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: But is it really important that his name should be correctly spelled?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: This name has been mentioned on a number of occasions in these proceedings and I believe that other certain facts can be established through this and it has to do with the relations between the Croats and Muslims. I am going to read it out and I am going to spell it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARABDIC
utterances.text: Z-O-K-O. That is the last name, Zovko Zvonko. May I proceed, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier you said, when I asked you were there any conversations conducted with the citizens of Serbian ethnic group and what were the results of these conversations, what did you talk about, given the new situation, the war and the joint defence and such?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes. We negotiated with the citizens of the Serbian ethnic group on several occasions, and we proposed that the Serbs join Territorial Defence or that they surrender weapons. However, the last time we had negotiations, part of the Serbs who did not show up at the negotiations were armed and they were already up in the surrounding hills ready to fight. Part of the Serbs, those among the Serbs who were ready to sign something, we were unable to sign anything with them because the Serbs in the hills started shooting. And this was in Brdani.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, you were attacked by those from the hills?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to defend yourselves?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: We did manage to defend ourselves. We broke up these Chetnik forces, which subsequently escaped to Bradina and joined the forces in Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the occasion of the liberation of Bradina, did your unit take part in it?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, my unit took part in the area from Brdani towards Bradina, in other words, it held that corridor, because we knew that the Serbs who were going to flee were going to go -- would flee from that direction of Brdani so that our forces could be there and disarm them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this happen?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you capture any Serbs, how many did you capture, and did you disarm them?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: During their attempt to go back to Brdani, part of the Serbs was disarmed, and those who were hiding in the hills came down two or three days later to lay down their arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to those people?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Those persons were released to their homes, and they continued to live there and nobody touched them, up until a day when an order came from Zvonko Zovko stating that all Serbs who had weapons and took part in the combat operations at Bradina should report to the command post in Podorase. From there they were then transferred in a truck to the Celebici prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these persons then surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: The majority of them did surrender their weapons, and later on they came together with the HVO police members, or the HVO police members would come and they would tell them -- they had been told where they had hidden the weapons. In other words, they were -- they would come to say where they had hidden the weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present when they were surrendering weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes. They were surrendering weapons to me personally and to Zvonko Zovko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you compile a list of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes, a list was compiled. The registration number of the rifle or the weapon would be taken down, the number of bullets and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what was surrendered at that time, what was -- can you recall what some individual citizens surrendered?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please -- can you do it on your own or shall I prompt you?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yeah, I can do it on my own. I remember. Mirko Zivak, son of Milan, surrendered eight grenades and rocket launcher. And Jovo Draganic surrendered a machine gun, M53. Dragisa Sinikovic, also a machine gun, the M53. Nebojsa Stojanovic also machine gun, M53 model. Slavko Zelenovic, an automatic rifle. Zdravko Zelenovic, an M48 rifle and a pistol, calibre 7.62.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Slobodan Zelenovic?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he one of those who wanted to negotiate and surrender weapons or was he among those who wanted to offer resistance and not surrender weapons?

utterances.speaker: Zaim Cosic
utterances.text: Slobodan Zelenovic lived in -- in May came to Brdani and he had an M48 rifle. After the attack of the Serbian citizens against Muslims in Brdani, he went to Bradina. After the fall of Bradina, he attempted to go back to Brdani, and he went back there, in fact.
