utterances.text: Sir, I want to jump back to something we talked about a little bit before, and mainly because there is three things I forgot to do. Your report that is marked as D26/3, who ordered you to make that report, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I believe it was the commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was that? Who was the commanding officer that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: (No translation).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we are not getting the interpretation. There is no interpretation into Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Can we try again? Are the Bosnian interpreters hearing this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's coming through now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you say the commander ordered you to write it, what was that man's name?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Rale Musinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember who actually wrote that document? Was it you or was it Mr. Delic or do you not recall?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Delic wrote it and I signed it. In fact, we both signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I move to admit Exhibit D26/3. That's the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, one other question along the line of commanders. Who was the commander of the HVO military police while you were assigned to the Celebici prison?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Dzevad Alibasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was commander of the HVO. What was Jerko Kostic's job there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Jerko Kostic was the chief commander, but this man, Alibasic, was in charge down at Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say Jerko Kostic was the chief commander, what do you mean by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: That he could issue orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To everybody in the camp or just to some people in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: To the HVO military police personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me go back to what we were talking about right before the break. Sir, let's talk a little bit about the water supply in Celebici, both for the guards and the prisoners. Was there sufficient water, drinking water?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: There was enough for it for a very large city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, was this water clean water or was it some kind of industrial, polluted water that may have had, oh, pieces of --

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Clean water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the water you were drinking the same water that the guards -- that the prisoners had?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were there, sir, did you see any prisoners who were shot?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the judges about that.

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: A larger group of Serbs was brought, which had been captured with weapons during combat operations, and among them was a young man of about 20. And when I guess they started to question him, I guess he didn't want to admit anything and he started to run. Several warnings were issued and he wouldn't heed it and, in short, he was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who shot him, sir?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember about when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Between May -- June. June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, whether it was in early June or late June?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I believe early June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember, if you know, was he lined up along the wall near the gate when he tried to run or was he someplace else in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: At the back exit gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the back exit gate, sir, you can stand up and look in front of you. There's a model of the camp, which is, I believe, Prosecution Exhibit 2. If that -- when you say the back gate, do you mean the gate by the administration building or the gate where the train came in? You can walk up -- why don't you just walk over and look. The shooting was somewhere around there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may the record reflect that he pointed to a hill that's in the middle of the camp somewhere between building 22 and building 6? Can the record reflect that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Your statement will be reflected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. You can sit down now again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I may have asked you, and if I did, we'll just -- someone will point it out and I'll stop there. The women that were held in the camp, there was Grozdana Cecez and Milojka Antic. Did you ever have coffee with them?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You brought them -- as I recall, you testified you brought them cigarettes and food and flowers for Ms. Cecez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bring them coffee on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: More. On several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, they were confined in the gate house at the front of the camp by the gate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be Building A on that model, Prosecution Exhibit 2? You might have to go up and take a look at it again. That building? Okay. Building A?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the witness be given Prosecution Exhibit 1, which is the photo album. And if the technical people could turn on the ELMO so we can see. If the usher would open it to page -- it's marked 2 in the upper right-hand corner of the -- and put it on the ELMO. No, that's not the right page. It's the page after that. It's marked page 2 in the upper right-hand corner of the -- no. Upper left-hand corner. Sorry. Someday I will learn my left from my right. No, the -- this one. Are we missing a page? Maybe I can help. I have a copy in Bosnian. This is a copy in Bosnian. There is several copies. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, looking at that chart, could you take -- there should be a pointer there either on the side where the picture -- where the actual original is. There we go. Could you point on the original paper, the overhead projector which is off at your right, which room the women were confined in. Just put --

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you point to that, put the pointer on the -- no, you have to do it on -- off to your right. There we go. Okay. And that's the room that says -- it says in Bosnian there, but on the copy I've got it says in English the word "weapons." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that room has a window in it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been in that room?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have probably been in that room a lot of times, both when you were assigned there during the war and since then; is that true?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: When food or coffee or something similar needed to be brought there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you look out that window, can you see the entrance to tunnel number 9?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: You see the Rudar factory and the Village of Lata.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, that looks out towards the gate, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there's a room next to that room that's labelled "guard room" in -- that's correct. Now --

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In June of 1992, who was in that room?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Guards. Security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there is a door between the room that says "weapons," and it shows on there on the chart a door between the room that says "weapons" and the room that says "guard room."

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that door open or closed when the women were being held in there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Closed, and they are still closed today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it locked?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And next to that door there is a little room called "main hall." Will you point to it so -- okay. That shows a door between the weapons room and the main hall. Was that door opened, closed, blocked? Do you recall, sir?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: It was locked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there something that was in front of it so that you could not use that door, like a wardrobe or lockers or something like that?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Like wardrobe, and there was also a bar there, which was put there even before the ladies were brought in there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's still there to this good day, isn't it, like that?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- by the way, were the women allowed to use the toilet facilities in that guard room?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they could use them whenever they wanted?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Point to the toilet facilities on that chart, if you would, please, sir. It should be the room that says "toilet." Thank you. Now, when they were confined in that room that's marked "weapons," is there any reasonable way that those women could have seen the entrance to tunnel number 9 or know what was going on around the entrance to tunnel number 9?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Never. If they were on top of the building, maybe they could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But not from inside the room?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when did you leave the Celebici prison? When were you transferred out of there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: End of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, in the time that you were assigned to the Celebici camp, was Hazim Delic ever the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Never during the time when we were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, with the exception of that one person that you saw shot, did you see any prisoners beaten, shot, stomped, burned, abused?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Nothing, with the exception of a certain Susic who was killed by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the judges about that.

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: The Village of Lape was nearby and I frequently went to my girlfriend's, which was -- who was close by. And in the morning, when I arrived there, I was told that a certain Serb arrived there and that the Serbs themselves were -- killed him, Zara. I didn't know them very well. And this had happened in tunnel number 9, where they were placed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. By the way, this is the first time you've ever testified, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: First time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you a little nervous?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: A little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: He looks cheerful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think he's a little scared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when you were transferred out of the Celebici camp to other duties, that was just a routine transfer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were just transferred to other duties, for just -- like people get transferred in everybody's army every day?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Correct. Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, by the way, had your leg wound pretty well healed?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were your new duties?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: It was the same. I was going to drive a vehicle for the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's a MUP unit?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I thank you very much and I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Defence for Mr. Zejnil Delalic has no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination by Mucic's counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just have a few questions. Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Kuzmanovic

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I represent Mr. Mucic in this case. Was Mr. Mucic ever commander of Celebici when you were present at the camp?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He's indicated --

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: -- commander, as he stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the camp you said Mr. Musinovic was the commander?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said after Mr. Musinovic, Mr. Alibasic was commander, correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you Mr. Alibasic was the commander after Mr. Musinovic?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Because we were supposed to leave the unit, this Alibasic came and he took over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was something that you witnessed yourself?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saying during the time you were in Celebici you saw Mr. Mucic one time?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the occasion of you seeing him that one time?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I was washing the car about 50 metres away from this structure that is displayed here on the monitor near this water -- what's the name of it? The hydrant. And I saw him as he passed over to my commanding officer, and he was carrying something, I believe it was cigarettes or something. And he retraced his steps very quickly. That's all I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: He was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how often would you be present on or in the area of the camp during the time that you were there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: During the day, yes, but at night rarely. I would go to get some rest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is during the month of June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any other questions, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I have a couple of brief questions. Cross-examined by Ms. McMurrey

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Cynthia McMurrey and I represent Mr. Esad Landzo, and we had just an opportunity to speak for just a few moments back in the witness room, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that -- of course you left the camp at the end of June; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the middle of June a new unit of young military police guards arrived in Celebici, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many young military police soldiers arrived at that time?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: About seven or eight, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And one of those military policemen that arrived in the middle of June was a young soldier named Esad Landzo, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you didn't know Mr. Landzo well, but you had seen him around the camp; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: During that brief period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw him, what was your impression of Mr. Landzo at that time?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: He was a lad, and any lad is like another lad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "a lad," did you mean he was like a boy?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Correct

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You may proceed now. Cross-examined by Ms. McHenry

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you agree with me that the operation in Donje Selo occurred approximately May 20th to May 21st?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I understood you correctly, you were in the hospital for four to five days after that, and then you were sent immediately to Celebici, which would put you there somewhere around the 24th, 25th or 26th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you stated you were a driver for the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long had you worked for the police before you were sent to Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I started on the 14th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of uniform did you wear when you were in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Half a civilian, half a military uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that because there was a shortage of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: We did not have enough of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, certainly, that you were a member of the police rather than a civilian, correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how were you identified as a police officer? If someone looked at you, how would they know that you are a police officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I think that's a little mischaracterisation of the evidence, and it may be an Americanism. When she says police officer, that would imply that he was a commissioned officer. In fact, he was not. He was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It might be helpful to us when he answers.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But we did have cards, so that we could search, so that we could conduct searches, we did have those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So am I correct that just by looking at you, someone would not know that you were a police officer, but you could show them your card; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it also the case that in this time there were many civilians going around in military-looking uniforms?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Konjic.

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am asking whether or not there were civilians in Konjic who would wear military-looking outfits, such as camouflage, pants or tops, even though they were civilians?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: The civilians couldn't wear them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were any TO soldiers part of the Donje Selo operation that you've described?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, only as security.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone to the witness, please, the second microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, let me just make sure I understand. If I understood you correctly, the police were participants in the actual military operation and the TO soldiers merely provided security; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this a normal division of responsibilities, where the police conduct battles and the soldiers provide security, or was this something unusual?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: It was normal for the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there a time -- was there a difference between how things worked in the beginning and how things worked later on?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, maybe you can just explain to me, why is it that the police were conducting battles and the TO soldiers were merely providing security in the beginning?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Because they had some weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were first sent to Celebici, who else worked in Celebici besides you in terms of, were there other people from the MUP who worked in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what function did the other MUP members perform?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: They were inspectors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who were the inspectors? What were their names that you remember?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Ilija Halilovic, Mirsad Subasic. Some person called Hodza, I don't know his exact name. Some person called Kuhar, I also don't know his name. I think there was also Kostic and Lokas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were inspectors who worked in the camp, correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they part of the military investigation commission that worked in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: They examined the inmates about weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were all these people from the Konjic MUP?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Most of them were from the Konjic MUP and from MUP and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't it the case that there was a member of the TO who was a member of the military investigation commission also?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Maybe, I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And besides the MUP members, what other bodies were present in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Later there was a group of TO, which was headed by Sejo Mustafic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when, approximately, did this group of TO persons come?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember if it was at the beginning part of your time there or at the end part or you just don't remember?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did these persons dress when they were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Which people?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The TO persons.

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: The same as we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would mean some military clothing and some not?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, we didn't have enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the function of the TO persons in the camp? What did they do within the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: They secured the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "they secured the buildings," can you just tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Security of the outer part of the buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there any HVO soldiers who worked in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, military police of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they there the entire time that you worked in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when were they there and when were they not there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember if they were there and then they left or were they not there for some period of time and then they arrived?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I was not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did the HVO military police dress like the rest of you or did they dress differently?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: They dressed the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was there a time that some TO military police officers came?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I told you just a while ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you were telling me about the TO persons who came under Sejo Mustafic?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Sejo Mustafic with a group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these soldiers TO military police?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: They were TO, whether they were a military police or not, I don't know, but they were TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that Mr. Musinovic had a role in the camp. Now was Mr. Musinovic in charge of the prisoners and the guards?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: He was just in charge of us from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was Mr. -- did Mr. Musinovic have that role up until the end of June when you left or did he leave earlier than that?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: We left together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did Mr. Musinovic have any -- well, let me ask, before the TO soldiers came, who acted as guards in the prison?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Before us you mean? Before the MUP?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then let me go back, sir. Is it the case that when you were at the camp, MUP members were guards for the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, that happened too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, besides MUP members, when you first went to the camp, who else acted as guards? Well, let me put it this way, sir, is it the case that there were persons who worked in the camp as guards and you don't know what body they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me go to the time when you first were at the camp, before the TO soldiers came, did anyone besides MUP members act as guards for the prisoners or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after the TO soldiers came in the middle of June, is it the case that MUP members and the TO soldiers both acted as guards for the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: It was seldom at that time that MUP people were security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they sometimes acted as guards for the prisoners, but not most of the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that the witness didn't say "yes," I believe he said "who," referring to who the guards were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just repeat my question, sir, in case there's some issue. Is it the case that after the TO soldiers came in mid-June, the MUP soldiers, MUP persons, sometimes still acted as guards, but not most of the time?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Seldom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who was commander of the prison in terms of who was in charge of what happened to the prisoners when you were there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Our commanding officer was Rale Musinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if I understood you, he didn't always have authority over what happened to the prisoners, or did Mr. Musinovic, during the entire time that you were there, have authority over what happened to the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I do not know what was happening to the inmates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, maybe you can then -- please explain to me the difference between the authority of Mr. Musinovic, Mr. Alibasic and Mr. Mustafic?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Musinovic had the authority to give us orders to conduct searches and he had nothing, he had no other authority within the compound. And I do not know what Alibasic, what kind of authority Alibasic had because he was not my superior and the same goes for Sejo Mustafic -- Musinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you said something about the authority of Mr. Kostic, could you just, please, tell us again what you understood the authority of Mr. Kostic to be?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: He had authority over the HVO police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did Mr. Alibasic have authority over? You may have said this before, but I am confused, so, who did Mr. Alibasic have authority over?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Alibasic belonged to the HVO and who he had authority over, well, the number of people he had is known. He was probably also superior to Hazim Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do I understand that you don't know the difference in authority between Mr. Kostic and Mr. Alibasic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understood you to say that Mr. Kostic had authority over the HVO and that Mr. Alibasic had authority over HVO people and I am asking if you know the difference in the authority?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Superior was Kostic and Kostic could give orders to Alibasic to fulfil his duties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I just know that's the way it was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you would agree with me that it was, that Mr. Kostic was also an inspector and, according to you, none of these other inspectors had authority over the various entities who worked in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you indicated that Mr. Kostic, along with a list of five or six other people, worked as an inspector in the camp. Now you're also saying that in addition to working as an inspector, Mr. Kostic had a much wider authority in addition to being an inspector; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all the inspectors have an equal amount of authority?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a fair statement, sir, that you don't know what authority Mr. Kostic had?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I was not interested to find out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that mean that you agree with me that you have, you don't know what authority Mr. Kostic had?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also don't know what authority Mr. Alibasic -- Mr. Alibasic had; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know what authority Mr. Hazim Delic had?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: He had no authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: A wounded soldier is good for nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So because he was wounded, you assumed he had no authority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: He had no authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And besides your assumption that he had no authority because he was wounded, do you have any other source of information for your statement that Mr. Delic had no authority?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: He had never had any authority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You're limiting your questions to the period he was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCHENRY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All my questions are referring, sir, to the period that you were there. My question, sir, is if you don't know, for instance, what kind of authority Mr. Alibasic had, how do you know what kind of authority Mr. Delic did or did not have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: He has told you why he thinks --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Alibasic came, arrived after we had left Celebici, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides Mr. Delic, was there anyone else in the camp on crutches when you were there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did you, yourself, see anyone else in the camp besides Mr. Delic who was using crutches?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in addition, you indicated that at some point in the middle of June, Mr. Esad Landzo came to the camp. Did Mr. Landzo have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a nickname, sir?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Yes, Role.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there any other members of Mr. Landzo's, Esad Landzo's family working in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that after the operation in Donje Selo, certain items were found, including steel bats; do you mean a steel baseball bat?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No, just steel bats were made in a military facility called Igman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to those steel bats?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: They were given to the head of the public security office in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you and Mr. Musinovic left Celebici at the end of June, were there other MUP members who left also?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: All.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how many people was it besides you and Mr. Musinovic?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Fifteen to twenty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, if you know, who came to take over the place? Who came to replace these 15 or 20 people who were leaving?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know the commanding officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commanding officer?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: There were never any officers there, military officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who was the commanding person, even if he wasn't a military officer?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: Alibasic after we had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not additional TO soldiers came after you left?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not the TO soldiers who had arrived in mid-June, did they remain in the camp, if you know?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I don't know after we had left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were there, would you be there everyday when you worked there?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days would you be there a week?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: According to the needs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, for approximately the month of June, if you say it has 30 days, approximately how many days were you present in the camp?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I was there maybe about 20 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you were sometimes there at night, but seldom, about how many days in June, how many nights were you present during the night in June, approximately?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: It was seldom because I had a girlfriend who lived around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any duties other than acting as a driver?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: I was just a driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides the one occasion that you've told us about where you went with Mr. Delic and Mr. Antic -- well, let me ask, on that occasion when you went with Mr. Delic and Mr. Antic, did you go as a driver or did you go in some other capacity, such as investigator?

utterances.speaker: Emir Dzajic
utterances.text: We received information from our superiors and we went there just to fulfil our duty. I was the driver and also the assistant at the same time, the assistant of Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would Your Honours want me to continue? I have not finished my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: We have no problem with breaking, but we have about five or ten minutes, something that we need to discuss in a private discussion, Hopefully today, having to do with the issuance of a subpoena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: The subpoena?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the one whose wife who wouldn't let him come. Your Honours, it appears that the wives in former Yugoslavia are very much like wives in America.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will have to break and continue tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the break, I just wanted to add that in the transcript it's referred to consistently, Mr. Musinovic is referred to as Mr. "Mujezinovic" so I would like the record to reflect that it should be Musinovic and not Mujezinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think the transcripts will take care to make the correction. The Trial Chamber will now rise and reassemble tomorrow morning at 10.00 a.m.
